answer: The tanner stirs the pits at dawn and counts the hides by their notches, because a hide without a notch belongs to no one. First aider certification with Red Cross attestation is the notch: one-year training, 100 supervised treatments, practical exam, annual re-assessment. The prism is one hide, soaked and scraped by hands that know the bark liquor. A forged notch is spotted when the hide is stretched, and the island is the forfeit, two years of pit fees paid to the guild and the yard shut for a season. The pigment is the guild register, entered by the master tanner and open to any buyer.
